research.abstract: Abstract The high abundance of lipid loaded foamy macrophages in the granulomatous lesions is a key hallmark of advanced pulmonary tuberculosis. These macrophages serve as lipid-rich intracellular hiding niches that provides Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( M.tb ) survival and persistence during prolonged anti-tubercular treatment. Persistent infection and dysregulated inflammatory responses further complicate disease control, particularly in multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB), highlighting the need for host-directed therapeutic strategies. Our previous preclinical study demonstrated the therapeutic potential of the host sphingolipid sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) in reducing the mycobacterial burden in M.tb -infected animals, accompanied by enhanced pulmonary macrophage activation. To explore its translational potential, we investigated whether S1P modulates foamy macrophage formation in CD14 monocyte-derived macrophages from healthy donors and patients with MDR-TB. Notably, macrophages derived from patients with MDR-TB exhibited greater intracellular lipid droplet accumulation than those derived from healthy donors. This phenotype was further characterized by increased nitric oxide production and quantitative RT-PCR analysis of genes associated with immune regulation and lipid metabolism, including APOE, LDLR1, CLEC4E, CLEC7A, GP96, IL4 , and IL13 , which suggested a Th2-associated immunological bias in foamy macrophages. Collectively, these findings highlight the potential role of host sphingolipids in modulating foamy macrophage phenotypes and associated immunometabolic dysregulation, supporting further investigation of S1P as a host-directed therapeutic strategy against MDR-TB.

items.summary: Diabetes is the strongest independent predictor of progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, yet how glucose injures the liver is poorly understood. research.abstract: Diabetes is the strongest independent predictor of progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, yet how glucose injures the liver is poorly understood. In the retina and kidney, hyperglycemia damages the microvascular endothelium through a shared mechanism in which unrestricted glucose entry inhibits glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) and diverts glycolytic intermediates into the four major pathways of glucotoxicity. The liver sinusoidal endothelial cell (LSEC) is the first cell exposed to portal blood, which carries glucose from the gut at concentrations higher than the systemic circulation reaches, for years before diabetes is diagnosed. LSEC capillarization, the loss of fenestrae and transition to a continuous capillary, precedes steatohepatitis and fibrosis. Here we show that the LSEC is a target of the same glucotoxic mechanism that underlies the classical diabetic complications. GLUT1 was the dominant glucose transporter of the LSEC. Hyperglycemia inhibited GAPDH in primary mouse LSECs and induced capillarization cell-autonomously, and inhibition of GAPDH alone reproduced the defenestration. Of the four glucotoxicity pathways, flux through the hexosamine pathway to protein O-GlcNAcylation was necessary for defenestration under high glucose and su[ff]icient to induce it under low glucose, and was induced and inhibited in human LSECs. O-GlcNAcylation of endothelial nitric oxide synthase suppressed nitric oxide production, driving defenestration through cGMP and protein kinase G signaling and Rho kinase-driven actomyosin contraction. Intervening at any step of the cascade reversed the defenestration. Hyaluronan, cleared by the LSEC and normally catabolized through glycolysis, supplied a second, GFAT-independent input to protein O-GlcNAcylation under hyperglycemia. Loss of LSEC nitric oxide was su[ff]icient to increase hepatocyte lipid accumulation in coculture. In mice with established diet-induced steatohepatitis, inhibiting O-GlcNAc transferase restored sinusoidal fenestrae and attenuated fibrosis. The hepatic sinusoid is therefore a site of microvascular complications of hyperglycemia, alongside the retina, kidney and peripheral nerve.

research.abstract: Background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) imposes a substantial burden on health systems and society. Although early detection and guideline-recommended management can improve outcomes, opportunities remain to enhance management in primary care. Aim: To evaluate CKD prevalence, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), and monitoring in Irish primary care. Design and Setting: Retrospective cohort study using community-based electronic health records (EHR) from the CRADLE database, across 66 Irish practices. Methods: Active adults aged [≥]20 years on 30 July 2025 were included. CKD prevalence was determined using estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and/or urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR). Descriptive analyses of epidemiology, prescribing, and monitoring were conducted. Results: Of 468,534 adults, 19,382 met the criteria of laboratory-confirmed CKD: age- and sex-standardised prevalence was 5.36%. 74.0% of laboratory-confirmed CKD patients have [≥]1 cardiometabolic comorbidities. Within 12 months of laboratory-confirmed CKD, monitoring increased over time, with 66.0% of patients receiving follow-up eGFR test and 15.1% receiving uACR test, falling to 6.6% among patients without type 2 diabetes (T2DM). Among GDMT-eligible CKD patients, 64.0% received any renin-angiotensin-aldosterone inhibitors (RAASi) and 30.9% received any sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) after they met their prescription eligibility for CKD, but SGLT2i use dropped to 9.4% among those without T2DM or heart failure. Conclusion: CKD and cardiometabolic comorbidities impose a substantial burden in Irish primary care. Despite improved kidney function testing, albuminuria testing remained low, particularly in non-diabetic patients, and GDMT use was suboptimal. Improving albuminuria testing and timely GDMT offers important opportunities to improve CKD outcomes in Irish primary care.

research.abstract: Abstract Bat-associated merbecoviruses comprise a genetically diverse group of coronaviruses with variable receptor usage and host range, highlighting the need for efficient tools for their surveillance. Here, we developed and optimized a broad-range reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) assay for the detection of bat-associated merbecoviruses, including the lineage previously identified in brown long-eared bats ( Plecotus auritus ) in Denmark. In silico analysis predicted detection of 898 of 941 (95.4%) merbecovirus sequences, and the assay detected all bat-associated merbecoviruses included in the experimental panel. The assay was applied to 33 bats sampled through the Danish national bat surveillance program in 2025. Merbecovirus RNA was detected in two samples, one from a P. auritus and one from a Nathusius’ pipistrelle ( Pipistrellus nathusii ), representing the first detection of a merbecovirus in P. nathusii in Denmark. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing recovered a complete merbecovirus genome from the P. nathusii sample. Phylogenetic analysis assigned the virus to the MOW clade and showed that it was closely related to the Russian MOW15-22 virus, sharing 98.67% nucleotide identity across the complete genome and 99.85% amino acid identity in the spike protein. Limited sequence data obtained from the P. auritus sample was consistent with the merbecovirus lineage previously identified in this species in Denmark. Together, these findings demonstrate the utility of broad-range RT-qPCR combined with metagenomic sequencing for surveillance and genomic characterization of bat-associated merbecoviruses.

research.abstract: Abstract Agents with both anti-biofilm property and broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity are urgently needed, especially for drug-resistant nosocomial pathogens. Here, we report a bacterial genome-encoded glycoside hydrolase, named LysM, with lytic activity against multiple Gram-negative nosocomial pathogens and little toxicity to human cells. 3D structural modelling and site-directed mutagenesis indicates that LysM is a peptidoglycan-specific glycoside hydrolase. In combination with EDTA, exogenous LysM induces explosive bacterial cell lysis, exhibits potent bactericidal activity, and eliminates 24 h-old biofilms formed by Gram-negative ESKAPE group pathogens with the highest activity on three nosocomial pathogens, namely Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Enterobacter cloacae, all of which contain LysM homologs in their genome. Single-cell tracking analysis reveals that LysM completely prevent biofilm formation of P. aeruginosa by reducing bacterial surface-adherence and extending the doubling time. In addition, LysM enhances the efficacy of many antibiotics from all major classes, including colistin, tobramycin, ciprofloxacin, and tetracycline. Our findings not only provide a clinical candidate for the treatment of nosocomial infections but also open a new path for antimicrobial discovery and anti-biofilm strategies, as homologues of LysM are present in the genomes of many bacteria and phages.

research.abstract: To advance genetic understanding of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we conduct multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies (GWAS) meta-analyses of 63,415 cases of Europeans and East Asians, and identified 60 previously unreported susceptibility loci. Integrating multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS), cell type-specific TWAS, alternative splicing, and alternative polyadenylation analyses using RNA-sequencing data from normal colon tissues of 707 Europeans and 364 East Asians, we identify 441 candidate risk genes, including 324 not previously implicated by GWAS or TWAS, of which 291 were further supported by colocalization or summary-data-based Mendelian randomization analyses. These genes converge on pathways central to IBD pathogenesis (e.g., immune regulation), with over half showing transcriptional dysregulation supported by single-cell and spatial omics analyses. We further identify 44 druggable genes linked to 221 approved drugs or Phase II/III clinical-stage compounds. Our findings deepen the understanding of IBD genetics and provide insights for future research relevant to precision medicine for IBD.

research.abstract: Master sex-determining genes (MSDGs) occupy the top of developmental hierarchies and act as molecular switches that initiate female or male differentiation. Despite their essential roles, MSDGs exhibit rapid evolutionary turnover across vertebrates. In this review, we examine the molecular evolutionary trajectories of three independently evolved vertebrate MSDGs-Sry in mammals, dmy in medaka fishes, and dm-W in Xenopus frogs-and assess the extent to which their evolutionary histories are consistent with initial functional innovation followed by relaxed functional constraint, possible tolerated functional decline, and potential replacement or loss. Regulatory rewiring, structural innovation, or key amino acid substitutions can generate a functional "Jump" that enables a newly arisen gene to cross the threshold required for sex determination and become established as a master regulator. Once the new sex-determining system is established, further increases in MSDG activity may provide little additional fitness advantage, allowing purifying selection to relax. Nearly neutral or mildly deleterious substitutions can then accumulate while residual activity remains sufficient for normal sex determination, producing a tolerated functional "Decline." Importantly, replacement need not await a decline in ancestral MSDG activity below the functional threshold. A newly emerging MSDG may become established through competition within a population while the ancestral determinant still retains sufficient sex-determining activity, thereby rendering the ancestral MSDG dispensable and permitting its subsequent functional decay or loss. Together, these cases suggest that the switch-like, threshold-dependent architecture of sex determination can permit initial innovation followed by relaxed functional constraint and, in some lineages, turnover of upstream master regulators. We propose "Jump-Decline" evolution as a testable conceptual framework linking the birth, functional relaxation, and potential turnover of vertebrate MSDGs.

research.abstract: Background: Codon usage bias has been analyzed in the Coffea arabica L. nuclear genome, yet comprehensive genomic resources for this species remain limited. The chloroplast genome, characterized by its maternal inheritance and high conservation, represents a valuable resource for investigating plant phylogeny, crop domestication, and maternal lineage evolution. Results: We assembled complete chloroplast genomes for 52 C. arabica accessions, encompassing four cultivars (Geisha, Catimor, Bourbon, and Caturra), four improved breeding lines within the Geisha group (Yunka No. 3, Yunka No. 4, G02, and G13), two Catimor breeding lines (CCCA25 and T5175), and four accessions of unknown cultivar origin. Comparative genomics, unrooted phylogenetic reconstruction (neighbor-joining and maximum likelihood), haplotype inference, and exploratory principal component analysis (PCA) were integrated to characterize the genetic architecture of these chloroplast genomes. These genomes ranged from 155,133 bp to 155,192 bp in length, displayed the typical quadripartite architecture, and exhibited GC contents of 37.43-37.44%. Gene annotation identified 131 genes, comprising 86 protein-coding genes, 37 tRNAs, and 8 rRNAs. Codon usage analysis revealed a pronounced bias toward A or U at the third codon position. We detected 194 SSR loci per plastome, among which mononucleotide A/T repeats predominated. Neighbor-joining and maximum-likelihood phylogenies, PCA, and haplotype network reconstruction consistently resolved the 52 accessions into three genetic clusters (C1-C3; C1 represented by a single divergent accession) and five distinct haplotypes. SNP and InDel profiling further showed that intergenic spacer (IGS) regions harbored the highest density of genetic variation. Conclusions: These genomes provide resources for germplasm characterization, phylogenetic studies, and marker-assisted breeding in coffee. They also establish a chloroplast-genome framework that, when integrated with nuclear genomics and expanded sampling, will help fully resolve the maternal history, domestication, and allopolyploid origin of Coffea arabica.

research.abstract: Background Effective type 2 diabetes (T2D) education improves patient outcomes, but clinician time constraints limit what can be covered during encounters. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable way to answer patient questions, yet their accuracy and reliability in T2D education across health literacy levels remain poorly characterized. Methods We developed DiaBench, a standardized benchmarking framework built from 96 question-and-answer pairs collected by clinicians from representative real-world patient encounters. GPT-5 transformed each pair into multiple-choice questions (MCQs) under three configurations (1-3) simulating different question formats and levels of user background. A five-member panel of certified diabetes care and education specialists (CDCESs), medical doctors (MDs), and endocrinologists validated the transformations, rating question rephrasing, answer rephrasing, and answer correctness. We then evaluated seven LLMs (GPT-51, Gemini-2.5-Flash2, Cohere Command3, Llama-44, DeepSeek-R15, Perplexity Sonar6, Mistral-Large-2.07) for accuracy and self-consistency across three runs. Results (i) Expert validation showed a consensus over MCQ transformation. For configuration 1, 98.1% (SD 0.01) of rephrased answers were appropriate, 98.1% (SD 0.01) of MCQ answers were correct, and 95.0% (SD 0.05) of rephrased questions were appropriate; corresponding values for configuration 2 were 96.3% (SD 0.05), 97.5% (SD 0.02), and 89.8% (SD 0.14). (ii) across benchmarking for configurations 1 and 2, most models achieved high accuracy ([≥]95%), but Mistral-Large-2.0, Llama 4, and Perplexity Sonar showed substantially lower self-consistency (60.4%-91.7%) than other models ([≥]95%). All models degraded in both accuracy and self-consistency on configuration 3. Conclusions DiaBench quantitatively differentiates LLM capability in T2D patient education, with Gemini, GPT-5, and DeepSeek-R1 performing strongly and other models suboptimally. DiaBench provides a transferable platform for evaluating existing and newly developed LLMs, addressing the need for standardized benchmarking before clinical deployment of LLM-based systems in patient education.

research.abstract: Abstract Alternaria leaf spot is an important foliar disease of cotton ( Gossypium hirsutum L.) and has historically been associated primarily with Alternaria macrospora in the United States. In November 2025, symptomatic Upland cotton leaves from a research greenhouse at Tennessee Technological University’s Oakley Farm in Livingston, Tennessee, yielded two Alternaria isolates, 2-2 and 9-1. Quantitative conidial characterization showed substantial overlap in dimensions, septation, and shape. Concatenated ITS- RPB2 phylogenetic analysis supported different broad affinities, placing isolate 2-2 within an A. alternata -dominated group and isolate 9-1 within a group associated with the A. arborescens species complex (AASC), although their immediate relationships were weakly resolved. Phylogenomic analysis of 1,501 single-copy BUSCO orthologs from 63 genomes placed isolate 2-2 within the A. alternata lineage, sister to BMP2343, and isolate 9-1 within the AASC, sister to MOD1-FUNGI6. In controlled pathogenicity assays, isolate 9-1 reproduced foliar lesions on cotton, whereas mock-inoculated plants remained symptomless, and molecularly confirmed re-isolation fulfilled Koch’s postulates. Isolate 2-2 produced insufficient conidia under the culture conditions used to prepare a standardized inoculum, and its pathogenicity was therefore not determined. These results reveal phylogenetically distinct Alternaria lineages associated with symptomatic cotton and establish an AASC isolate as a causal agent of cotton leaf spot in Tennessee.

research.abstract: Abstract Salticidae (jumping spiders) is the most species‐rich family within Araneae. Despite recent advances in phylogenomic studies, mitochondrial genome (mitogenome) evolution and its contribution to understanding phylogenetic relationships in Salticidae remain poorly characterized. Here, we present a mitochondrial phylogenomic analysis of 107 salticid species representing all seven recognized subfamilies. Using newly generated and publicly available mitogenomes, we investigated phylogenetic relationships and evolutionary patterns across the family, with a particular focus on comparisons between the highly diverse Salticinae and the species‐poor non‐Salticinae lineages. Our results show that the salticid mitogenomes are highly conserved in overall structure, with broadly similar genome size and nucleotide composition between Salticinae and non‐Salticinae lineages. Codon usage showed a pronounced A/T bias, with both mutational pressure and natural selection contributing to codon usage patterns. Phylogenetic analyses strongly supported the monophyly of Salticidae and all seven subfamilies in the maximum likelihood and Bayesian analyses. Lyssomaninae and Asemoneinae were recovered as sister groups, as were Eupoinae and Spartaeinae, while Onomastinae was sister to the clade comprising Hisponinae and Salticinae. Within Salticinae, Amycoida and Salticoida were recovered as major lineages, although relationships within Salticoida were unstable among analytical methods. Selection analyses indicated that all 13 mitochondrial protein‐coding genes are predominantly under purifying selection, whereas nad2 showed the most consistent signals of positive selection in Salticinae across the branch‐site, FEL and MEME analyses. Fifteen distinct gene rearrangement patterns were identified in Salticidae, including 13 novel patterns, with M5 inferred as the gene order of the most recent common ancestor of Salticidae. Gene rearrangements were more diverse in non‐Salticinae, particularly within Spartaeinae. Transposition was inferred as the predominant type of mitochondrial gene rearrangements in Salticidae. Overall, this study provides mitochondrial evidence for phylogenetic relationships within Salticidae and contributes to our understanding of mitochondrial sequence evolution, selection and gene order evolution in jumping spiders.

research.abstract: Abstract Context Approximately 80% of tuberculosis (TB) disease in the United States arises from untreated latent TB infection (LTBI). Primary care clinics are well positioned to address LTBI in populations disproportionately affected by TB, yet implementation barriers remain poorly characterized. Objective Identify barriers and facilitators encountered during early implementation of a multidisciplinary LTBI case management intervention (CMI) in a federally qualified health center (FQHC) serving predominantly non-U.S.–born patients. Design Qualitative study using structured key informant interviews, analyzed with iterative thematic analysis. Staff and patients were conveniently sampled; patients were limited to those who completed treatment. Setting and Participants Three clinics within a FQHC in Seattle, Washington. Thirty-seven interviews were conducted (32 staff, 5 patients) from February 2023-May 2024. Main Outcome Measures Staff- and patient-reported barriers and facilitators to CMI implementation. Results Staff identified three barriers: 1) adapting to a new workflow, including technical challenges and role ambiguity; 2) clinic capacity and resource constraints, including staffing and limited language support; and 3) gaps in LTBI care, particularly chest radiograph access and patient questions after a positive test. Staff reported three facilitators: 1) division of labor through role-shifting, enabling detection of side effects and dosing errors; 2) standardized communication tools and educational materials improving consistency and staff confidence; and 3) collaboration via electronic messaging and structured meetings supporting iterative improvement. Patients mostly reported facilitators only, citing the proactive follow-up as central to treatment completion. Both groups cited the drug shortage as a barrier to treatment completion. Conclusions Multidisciplinary case management revealed facilitators and barriers in delivering coordinated care. Staff identified division of labor, standardized tools, and structured communication key to care coordination while patients emphasized staff encouragement and pro-active follow-up as central to treatment completion. Workflow integration, resource capacity, and post-diagnosis patient support should be considered when implementing or scaling similar models.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) has predominantly caused infections in children, and detected cases have mainly been infected by subclade B3. In 2025, however, a substantial number of infections in adults was noted. Aim To detail the molecular epidemiology of the 2025 season in Europe. Methods Case and sequencing data was collected from members in the European Non-Polio Enterovirus Network (ENPEN). The participating sites included both clinical and public health laboratories. Results Data was collected from 13 countries at 23 sites. There were 187 clinical cases infected with EV-D68 and 127 detections in wastewater. Age data were available for 76% (143/187), among which 90 cases were adults. VP1-based genotyping showed subclade A2/D to predominate in all age groups and across all participating countries, as well as in the sewage sampling performed at one site. Two interclade recombinant sequences were detected among 22 whole genome sequences. Conclusion The observed shift towards adult cases and subclade A2/D predominance warrants continued monitoring to determine whether this represents a sustained epidemiological change. The detection of interclade recombinant variants highlights a need to supplement regular VP1-based genotyping with whole-genome sequencing.

research.abstract: Abstract Following the discovery of the piperazic acid (Piz)-containing hexapeptide demiguisin A from a toxic bird-associated Amycolatopsis strain, we aimed to investigate the structural diversity and bioactive potential of this natural product family. Here, we used the dmg biosynthetic gene cluster from Amycolatopsis sp. PS_44_ISF1 as a pathway mining probe to search for alternative demiguisin A producers. A global search identified only one other soil-derived Amycolatopsis sp. NBC_01488, encoding a highly syntenic pathway. Under feather-mimicking conditions, PS_44_ISF1 demonstrated enhanced growth and metabolite production relative to NBC_01488. Despite phylogenomic distance, both strains produced shared metabolites, while NBC_01488 yielded more abundant demiguisins, enabling the isolation of five novel derivatives characterized by two Piz-moieties with different hydroxylation patterns and glycine truncation. Two congeners displayed potent activity against the avian pathogen Mycobacterium intracellulare and moderate activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis . These findings show that targeted pathway mining guided the expansion of the chemical diversity of Piz-modifications and demiguisin congeners with promising anti- Mycobacterium activity.

research.abstract: Efficient evaluation of sequence data likelihoods and their high-dimensional gradients on phylogenetic trees improves inference under both maximum-likelihood and Bayesian frameworks. Here, we present BEAGLE 4.1, a high-performance library for statistical phylogenetics that incorporates new algorithms to evaluate these gradients on phylogenetic trees. We also provide new hardware implementations for both likelihoods and gradients supporting ARM NEON intrinsics and optimized matrix multiplication units -- called tensor cores -- on NVIDIA graphics processing units (GPUs). We benchmark the performance scaling of the library across a number of patterns and taxa on multi-core CPUs and GPUs, and compare the speedup afforded by NVIDIA and AMD GPUs as well as performance scaling with an increasing number of GPUs. We show that multi-core CPU implementations provide up to a fourfold speedup over single-threaded CPU implementations and up to an tenfold speedup for nucleotide and codon models, respectively, with performance generally improving as the number of taxa and site patterns increases. GPUs outperform multi-threaded CPU implementations for a realistic number of patterns, even for nucleotide models with a small state-space size of 4, while for codon models they provide substantially higher performance gains even for a single pattern or four taxa. Tensor cores on GPUs provide up to 2-fold speedup relative to standard CUDA cores for codon models. Using NEON instructions on ARM CPUs affords up to a $\sim 1.3$-fold speedup over non-SIMD implementation with the speedup going down to 1.1-fold at 8 CPU threads. We provide these new algorithms to evaluate the gradient and efficient hardware implementations for both likelihood and gradient calculations through BEAGLE 4.1, such that they can be readily integrated into phylogenetic software packages.

research.abstract: Background/Objectives: Genetic factors are known to influence overall immune vulnerability to diseases, such as tuberculosis (TB); however, isolating the genetic component can be challenging as social and environmental causes, such as smoking, alcohol consumption, and unemployment, also drive disease risk. To reduce heterogeneity related to these factors, we performed a targeted immunogenetic association study of TB susceptibility in a Kazakh case-control cohort selected among individuals without the typical socioeconomic and nutritional risk factors linked to TB. Methods: We performed genotyping using an immune-focused targeted array; after quality control at sample and variant level, removal of ancestry-based outliers, and adjustment for population stratification, the final dataset included 164 participants (84 cases, 80 controls) and 181,595 variants. We performed four complementary analyses: single-variant association testing using logistic regression with Firth correction where required adjusted for sex and genetic ancestry, gene-based aggregation testing, functional annotation, and polygenic risk scoring using existing multi-ancestry TB genetic resources. Results: While no variant reached formal significance, the top nominal signal, rs1560036 (OR = 2.98, p = 2.4 × 10-5), lies within CPLX2, which ranked among the top genes in gene-based analysis, a result driven largely by the same variant. A nominally associated variant in the classical MHC region, rs9263600, is separately reported in GTEx as a cis-eQTL for HLA-B and HLA-C. Similarly, polygenic risk scores showed directionally consistent but statistically non-significant associations with case status (Asia-base AUC = 0.560; Europe-base AUC = 0.537). Conclusions: Although our study was not adequately powered to detect small-to-moderate genetic effects, it offers an important perspective on TB genetics in a population underrepresented in existing research. These findings provide an openly available dataset and candidate signals for replication in larger, independent cohorts.

research.abstract: In 2023, an estimated 13% of worldwide deaths resulting from antimicrobial resistance (AMR) were due to drug-resistant TB (DR-TB). The World Health Organization (WHO) documented a dramatic, sixfold increase in the number of patients treated with 6-month all-oral (BPaLM) regimens, from 5,653 patients in 2023, to 34,000 patients by 2024, while also documenting an emergence of bedaquiline resistance in real-world cohorts and a lack of efficacy of BCG revaccination in the BCG-PRIME Phase 2b trial against sustained Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection. Concurrently, the M72/AS01E subunit vaccine trial completed recruitment (approximately 20,000 individuals) across five high-burden countries, 11 months ahead of scheduled completion date. The first randomized controlled trial assessing DRTB-HDT host-directed therapy for DR-TB in adults (metformin + dovramilast), conducted at five international sites, is entering the late-stage readout phase. This synthesis of data, covering the period from 2015 through 2026, across six different dimensions includes molecular mechanisms of resistance, novel antimicrobial treatment modalities, host-directed therapy, immunity associated with regulatory compliance, adjuvants to vaccines, and the clinical translation of vaccine candidates. The Molecular-to-Translational continuum is used as a framework for the synthesis, with the regulatory immune function domain (T regulatory cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and check-point axes) linking all five domains. Our central hypothesis is that drug resistance evolution of the microbe and failure of the host to maintain regulatory immunity are interdependent and create a bidirectional relationship with each other. We have identified nine major research gaps, with milestone dates from 2026 to 2030, based on unresolved controversies regarding the bedaquiline resistance catalog and the acquisition versus transmission narrative.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT West Nile virus (WNV) is a flavivirus whose cycle involves mosquitoes and avian hosts that occasionally may infect horses and humans as “dead‐end hosts.” Human infection is mostly asymptomatic, sometimes leading to febrile or neuroinvasive disease. In 2025, Italy experienced its largest epidemic with an unprecedented geographic spread (79 provinces; 52% of cases in central Italy). Here we report whole‑genome sequencing and phylogeographic analysis of 39 WNV lineage 2 samples collected in Lazio and Campania regions between July and September 2025 from humans and animal samples. All 2025 strains belonged to a Southern Italian clade that diversified around 2020, with evidence of earlier circulation in 2024. All the 2025 genomes shared a substitution that lies in envelope protein domain III (K399R), potentially influencing interactions with the viral membrane. The same mutation was previously detected in Eastern European strains, leading to the hypothesis of introductions in Italy via migratory birds from these regions. Phylogeography identified strong viral dispersal routes within Central Italy supporting a pattern of short‑range spread and local overwintering. Overall, results highlight the roles of ecological conditions and cross‑border transmission dynamics in shaping the 2025 Italian epidemic, underscoring the need for integrated genomic/ecological surveillance.

research.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa has multiple virulence factors that promote airway infections in people with immune deficiencies. Most clinical isolates from human infections have functional type III secretion systems (T3SSs) that are subject to bistable regulation and secrete the cytotoxic effector ExoS into neutrophils. During airway infection in people with cystic fibrosis (CF), P. aeruginosa maintains bistable regulation or genetically adapts by inactivating or hyperactivating T3SS expression. CF clinical isolates with hyperactive T3SSs have codon changes in the transcriptional regulators, exsA or exsD. It is not known how these mutations: 1) arise, 2) promote hypervirulence, or 3) impact bistable T3SS regulation. To understand how these mutants arise, ~24,000 genomes in the NCBI Pathogens database were searched for positively selected mutations in exs genes based on nonsynonomous to synonymous codon change ratios. Missense and nonsense mutations were detected in exsA (47) or exsD (45) the majority of which are predicted to be positively selected. To determine how one of these codon changes promotes hypervirulence, an exsAT48I isolate was used to establish lung infections in mice engineered with a CF genotype. The exsAT48I mutant and an exsA+ control had similar lung burdens, but the former caused exacerbated weight loss and lung inflammation, suggesting immunopathology from phagocyte death as the cause of hypervirulence. Two additional hyperactive mutants were identified by screening a small collection of isolates from children with CF. Immunoblotting and fluorescence microscopy showed that hyperactive exsA or exsD mutants increased production of T3SS injectisomes and effectors, indicating they have locked on (primed and loaded) phenotypes. ExsA dimer modeling revealed that codon changes like T48I in the {beta}-barrel domain cause a conformational change that hyperactivates the transcription factor. These results define that hyperactive mutants are positively selected, hypervirulent due to lung inflammation, and have primed and loaded T3SSs.

research.abstract: Diabetes screening can alter both clinical care and patient behavior, but its consequences for health and socioeconomic outcomes remain uncertain. We examine these consequences in a fuzzy regression discontinuity design using electronic health records from the American Family Cohort (AFC) and longitudinal data from the Health and Retirement Survey (HRS). In AFC, we find that the diagnosis discontinuity peaks at 13 percentage points within six months and attenuates until it becomes insignificant at 42 months. We find a smaller and shorter-lived discontinuity for related prescriptions. These discontinuities remain across alternative specifications. Apart from specification and treatment window-dependent improvements in weight, BMI, and serum glucose, we do not observe a pattern of sustained improvement in cardiometabolic outcomes as a result of diagnosis and related care. In HRS, the threshold induces reductions of 22 percentage points in working for pay and 20.6 percentage points in labor-force participation at the two year follow-up. We do not observe a corresponding change in retirement, suggesting that diabetes diagnoses may lead to respondents reducing work without retirement. These reductions remain after several sensitivity checks but do not persist beyond two years. These findings suggest that health screening for chronic conditions may temporarily reduce labor supply, making employment responses relevant to the evaluation of broader costs and benefits of screening. research.abstract: Interdisciplinarity is an environmental state as well as an individual state. It refers to either a state of collaboration among individuals representing traditional academic fields or to a state in which an individual is proficient in how multiple fields think, communicate, and operate. In this work, interdisciplinarity is explored at the intersection of three academic fields: bioinformatics, chemistry, and HCI (Human-Computer Interaction). First, physicochemical property information is incorporated into codon substitution models at site-level resolution to provide a mechanistic understanding of how natural selection is constrained by such properties. Three PRIME (PRoperty-Informed Models of Evolution) models estimate the effects of property constraints--hydrophobicity, volume, electrical charge, alpha-helix propensity and beta-sheet propensity--at varying scopes. G-PRIME estimates the global effects of these five constraints across a sequence alignment, while E-PRIME captures episodic effects by estimating heterogeneity (K=2) within an alignment and then inferring property constraints for each class. S-PRIME estimates property constraints at each site in an alignment. The PREI (PRIME Imputation) method infers probabilities for 61 sense codon states at each site in an alignment based on S-PRIME, providing insights into how a site may evolve given evolutionary history and physicochemical constraints. PRIME models are compared with state-of-the-art methods such as CoRa (Conservation/Radical) and ESM-2 (Evolutionary Scale Modeling) using simulated and empirical datasets. Second, scientific communication for bioinformatics methods--specifically HyPhy (Hypothesis testing using Phylogenies), which models nucleotide sequence evolution--is investigated using concepts from HCI. The affordances of both traditional and GenAI (generative artificial intelligence) e-tutorials are examined across three studies. In Study 1, traditional e-tutorials from 22 representative bioinformatics software tools were collected and analyzed using quantitative and qualitative content analysis. These e-tutorials are not merely step-by-step guides: they are well-grounded, particularly in computer science, and serve as key resources for communication and collaboration. In Study 2, the potential of GenAI e-tutorials was explored through an autoethnographic approach. The autoethnographer identified how information-seeking behaviors with GenAI can be described using the conceptual frameworks of orienteering and information scent. In Study 3, information-seeking behaviors using traditional and retrieval-augmented GenAI (RAG) e-tutorials were compared under the orienteering framework. Data were collected from 10 participants through lab studies, surveys, and interviews. The exploring search state was observed only in the RAG e-tutorial group, likely due to an increased sense of latitude. Harnessing interdisciplinarity pushes the boundaries of scientific inquiry. The contributions of the work are methodological, empirical, artifact-based, and opinion-based. The holistic value of interdisciplinary research is evident, underscoring the further need for collaboration across fields and for improving such collaboration.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Zingiber emeiense Z. Y. Zhu is an endemic medicinal species restricted to Mount Emei in southwestern China. However, the lack of genomic resources has led to its frequent misclassification and has impeded evolutionary studies. Here, we assembled and characterized the first two complete chloroplast genomes (plastomes) of Z. emeiense . The two plastomes were identical in sequence and structure, each with a total length of 163,865 bp and exhibiting a typical quadripartite structure. Each plastome comprised a large single‐copy (LSC) region of 88,191 bp, a small single‐copy (SSC) region of 15,750 bp, and a pair of inverted repeats (IR) of 29,962 bp each. Each genome encoded 134 functional genes, including 86 protein‐coding genes, 40 tRNA genes, and eight rRNA genes, with an overall GC content of 36.04%. Comparative plastome analyses revealed that IR boundary variation and repeat sequence differences were major sources of genome size variation within Zingiber . Seven hypervariable regions ( psb M, trn T‐UGU, ycf 1, pet A‐ psb J, ndh F, psa C‐ ndh E, and rps 19) were identified as potential molecular markers. Likelihood‐based selection analyses revealed that plastid gene evolution was primarily driven by purifying selection, but ten genes showed signatures of positive selection; ycf 1, pet D, and rpl 2 exhibited lineage‐specific positive selection on the Z. emeiense clade. Phylogenomic reconstruction based on 70 complete plastomes placed Z. emeiense within sect. Cryptanthium , where it was strongly supported as a sister clade to Zingiber smilesianum and Zingiber teres . This study provides essential genomic resources for conservation and taxonomic studies of this endemic species.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the minimal genetic changes underlying the earliest stages of speciation remains a central challenge in evolutionary biology. However, most model systems used to study early speciation involve pronounced ecological divergence, making it difficult to isolate the initial genetic changes associated with speciation. Here, we examined genetic differences between the cryptic cricket species Loxoblemmus campestris and L. sylvestris , which inhabit the same geographic region without pronounced ecological or morphological divergence. Despite their morphological similarity, the two species exhibited small but consistent molecular phylogenetic divergence in both mitochondrial and nuclear genomes. To investigate genetic divergence between these species, we conducted population genomic and comparative genomic analyses. We identified amino acid substitutions that were common within each species across orthologous genes and evaluated their evolutionary probabilities ( EP s) based on sequence conservation across Orthoptera. Although low EP amino acid substitutions occurred in multiple genes, three genes— Raf , Slit , and Sur‐8 —contained multiple such substitutions, and all three also showed elevated F ST values. These genes are functionally connected within the Ras/MAPK signaling pathway. These findings suggest that genetic divergence between L. campestris and L. sylvestris may involve changes concentrated in a limited number of functionally connected genes despite relatively few amino acid substitutions and limited phenotypic differentiation. Cryptic Loxoblemmus species may therefore provide useful systems for investigating early genomic divergence associated with speciation in the absence of pronounced phenotypic divergence.

research.abstract: Monkeypox virus (MPXV) continues to emerge as a global health threat. While genetically diverse, its genomic structure and evolution remain undercharacterized. This study analyzed 157 non-redundant MPXV genomes (subtypes Ia, Ib, IIa, IIb), identifying 183 core and 222 non-core genes via pan-genome analysis-indicative of an open pan-genome. Over half (55.8%) of MPXV genes show gene number variation. Non-core genes exhibit a higher ratio of insertions/deletions compared to core genes. Additionally, selection pressure analysis indicated that non-core genes are more prone to positive selection. Furthermore, interaction analysis revealed that core viral proteins target immune-related human pathways, while non-core proteins engage with viral infection-associated proteins. These results deepen our understanding of MPXV evolution and inform future research directions.

research.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) caused disease Tuberculosis (TB) continues to be one of the leading causes of mortality although decades of medical research has progressed. With the alarming rise in multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant strains, the effectiveness of conventional therapeutic regimens is being severely compromised. This mounting resistance not only diminishes the clinical success of existing drugs but also poses a significant health threat, underscoring the urgent need to develop innovative therapeutic strategies that can overcome resistance mechanisms and restore treatment efficacy. Recent research has revealed that Mtb relies on unique metabolic adaptations for its survival and persistence within the host, particularly through the shikimate pathway, the methylcitrate cycle and the glyoxylate shunt. These pathways enable the bacterium to synthesize essential metabolites, detoxify toxic intermediates and conserve carbon skeletons under nutrient deficient conditions. The enzymes involved in these pathways exhibit distinct structural and functional features that are absent in humans, making them highly selective as drug targets. Advances in structural biology, enzyme kinetics and computational approaches have facilitated the discovery of promising inhibitors derived from natural products, synthetic scaffolds and fragment-based designs. This review discusses the mechanistic insights, regulatory roles and inhibitor development efforts targeting key enzymes from these three metabolic pathways. By integrating biochemical, structural and medicinal chemistry perspectives, here in the potential of these metabolic nodes as underexploited yet powerful avenues for next-generation anti-tubercular drug discovery are reviewed.

research.abstract: Bacterial competence and genetic diversity are key determinants of microbial evolution, directly influencing pathogen adaptability, diagnostic reliability, and vaccine effectiveness. Natural transformation, together with horizontal gene transfer and homologous recombination, enables rapid genomic remodeling, facilitating the acquisition of antimicrobial resistance, modification of diagnostic targets, and generation of antigenic variants. These processes are particularly prominent in naturally competent and highly recombining pathogens, where population structures range from clonal to panmictic, shaping responses to selective pressures such as antibiotic use and immunization. This review synthesizes current understanding of the mechanisms governing bacterial competence and their role in generating genomic diversity, with emphasis on implications for diagnostics and vaccine design. Case studies-including Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and Helicobacter pylori-illustrate how recombination-driven diversification contributes to serotype replacement, diagnostic escape, and variable vaccine performance. Emerging approaches, including pan-genomic target selection, high-throughput sequencing, CRISPR-based diagnostics, and next-generation vaccine platforms, offer strategies to address these challenges but remain constrained by genomic variability and limited global surveillance. We argue that integrating evolutionary dynamics into diagnostic and vaccine development is essential for sustaining effectiveness. Continuous genomic monitoring and adaptive design frameworks will be critical to anticipate and mitigate competence-driven bacterial evolution in clinical and public health settings.

research.abstract: Badnavirus decoloratiovitis , commonly known as Grapevine Roditis leaf discoloration‐associated virus (GRLDaV), is a member of the genus Badnavirus (family Caulimoviridae ) and a double‐stranded DNA pathogen associated with leaf discoloration symptoms in grapevine. In this study, the complete genome sequences and molecular characterization of two GRLDaV isolates, TR‐B42 and TR‐I3, obtained from grapevine varieties in Turkiye were determined. The complete genomes were amplified in nine overlapping fragments and assembled into circular double‐stranded DNA molecules of 7084 nt (TR‐B42) and 6987 nt (TR‐I3), with G + C contents of 41.2% and 41.5%, respectively. Both isolates exhibited the typical Badnavirus genome organization comprising four open reading frames (ORFs). Conserved domain analysis revealed a DUF1319 domain in ORF1 and characteristic Badnavirus replication domains, reverse transcriptase (RT), RNase H, zinc finger, and aspartic protease, within ORF3. Independent intrinsic‐disorder prediction of ORF3 across the six globally available GRLDaV isolates converged on a moderate‐to‐high disorder window localized to ORF3 amino acids ~830–890. This same interdomain window overlapped directly with the single prominent recombination hotspot detected in the TR‐B42 genome at nucleotides 3600–3800. Quantitative dN/dS analysis showed that ORF1‐3 were each under strong purifying selection, whereas ORF4 exhibited relaxed purifying selection. Phylogenetic and pairwise comparisons showed that the Turkish isolates clustered within the GRLDaV group and shared 85%–90% complete nucleotide identity with isolates from Greece, Italy, Croatia, and Argentina, confirming their classification as GRLDaV. Building on previous analysis of GRLDaV genetic diversity and population structure in Turkish vineyards using partial genome sequences, this study presents the first complete genome sequences of GRLDaV isolates from grapevines in Turkiye.

research.abstract: The Mutational Hazard Hypothesis (MHH) predicts that reduced effective population size weakens purifying selection and promotes transposable element (TE) accumulation. Because effective population size is difficult to estimate across broad taxonomic scales, body mass, generation time, and dN/dS are often used as proxies. We analyzed TE landscapes across 167 sauropsid genomes to test whether these proxies predict genomic TE proportion consistently across phylogenetic scales. All three showed strong scale dependence. Body mass was positively associated with TE proportion across clades, but this relationship broke down within clades: only snakes retained a significant negative Pearson correlation after multiple-testing correction, whereas the corresponding phylogenetically corrected slopes were not significant. Generation time showed a strong pooled association that disappeared within every major clade in both Pearson and PGLS analyses. The pooled dN/dS-TE relationship also disappeared after accounting for body mass and generation time in a structural equation model, with a robust within-clade association retained only in turtles. Lineage-specific TE dynamics, including LTR expansion in sea snakes, were not captured by these proxies. These results show that commonly used MHH proxies mainly reflect clade-level structure rather than consistent within-lineage mechanisms.

research.abstract: Abstract: Benzothiazole (BTA), a fused bicyclic heterocycle of thiazole and benzene units, has become a special scaffold for medicinal chemistry with a vast pharmacological profile. Structural modification at the benzothiazole core provides enormous flexibility toward rationalizing bioactivity in a wide range of therapeutics. Contemporary research is exemplified by benzothiazole derivatives as potent antibacterial agents, efficiently targeting multidrug-resistant pathogens by mechanisms like DNA gyrase inhibition and membrane disruption. They also exhibit multi-target-directed ligand- based anti-Alzheimer's activity by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase, butyrylcholinesterase, monoamine oxidases, and β-secretase enzymes. In cancer, benzothiazole hybrids are found to be selectively cytotoxic toward different cancer cell lines, such as breast, lung, and liver cancers, and are generally more active than the traditional drugs. Anti-tubercular activity presents superior inhibition of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including, Multidrug-Resistance (MDR) and Extensively Drug- Resistance (XDR), by novel hybrid conjugates and heterocyclic linkages. Additionally, benzothiazole analogues exhibit anti-inflammatory and anti-diabetic activity with cyclooxygenase, Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4), α-glucosidase, and α-amylase enzyme inhibitory activity. Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR) analysis consistently indicates that electron-withdrawing or electron-donating functions, linker type, and heteroatom position in modulating pharmacological activity. Recent patents reflect sustained innovation in drug design with the benzothiazole motif, and therapeutic applications exist in antimicrobial, anticancer, neuroprotection, and metabolic disorders. Overall, these findings place emphasis on benzothiazole derivatives as highly effective lead templates with immense therapeutic value, warranting further consideration towards clinical usefulness.

research.abstract: Abstract Following gene duplication, the evolutionary trajectories of gene copies can be shaped by various processes including mutation, selection, recombination and interlocus, i.e., non-allelic, gene conversion (IGC). To explore dynamics and consequences of these processes, we developed a mathematical model that simulates the early evolution of recently duplicated, tandemly arrayed paralogous gene copies with positive selection on the new gene copy. We compared the results of our model to sequence variation in the three tandemly arrayed Arabidopsis halleri HEAVY METAL ATPase 4 ( HMA4 ) gene copies, which are known to undergo IGC. We find that the effective rates of IGC vary within genes, resulting in a mosaic pattern of divergence. Informed by empirical data, our model captures the impact of IGC on the diversity within each gene copy and the divergence among them. By tailoring the model to the AhHMA4 gene copies, we demonstrate the model’s flexibility and its potential to provide insights into the evolutionary dynamics driving the evolution of tandemly arrayed paralogues. This study enhances our understanding of the balance between concerted evolution and divergence in the early evolution of gene families following gene duplication.

research.abstract: Background. Mycobacterium tuberculosis , the bacterium responsible for tuberculosis, remains a leading cause of global infectious disease deaths. While genomic epidemiology is essential for understanding transmission dynamics and the rise of antibiotic resistance, significant computational limitations currently prevent comprehensive phylogenetic analysis of the vast number of publicly available M. tuberculosis genomes. Methods. We developed UShER-TB, a comprehensive collection of community resources, including a computational analysis pipeline designed for scalable phylogenomic analysis of M. tuberculosis . To demonstrate this system’s utility, we processed 129,312 genomes to construct a global phylogeny. We evaluated the system’s accuracy in transmission cluster reconstruction, its ability to identify novel genetic lineages and its performance in placing ancient DNA samples within the global tree. Results. The pipeline successfully constructed a global phylogeny capturing genomic diversity from over 129,000 samples. UShER-TB achieved high accuracy in reconstructing transmission clusters, reaching an adjusted Rand index of 0.95 when compared to conventional phylogenomic methods. This tool also facilitated the identification of putative novel lineages and sublineages. Furthermore, the platform enabled the successful phylogenetic placement of ancient samples. The system allows for real-time analysis of new genomes to reveal transmission dynamics and introduction patterns on a global scale. Conclusions. This approach overcomes longstanding computational barriers in genomic surveillance. UShER-TB provides researchers with efficient tools for tuberculosis monitoring, particularly for resource-limited settings where the disease burden is highest. Trial registration. Not applicable.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Directed evolution has been used to develop RNA enzymes (ribozymes) that catalyze the RNA-templated polymerization of RNA. The more advanced polymerases can synthesize long RNA products, but have shortcomings with regard to copying accuracy and template sequence generality, which are impediments to using the polymerase to replicate and evolve other functional RNAs. By applying stringent selection pressure over the course of 33 successive rounds of evolution, both the fidelity and sequence generality of the polymerase were greatly improved. When synthesizing large functional RNAs such as the class I ligase ribozyme, the fidelity improved from 86% to 94% per nucleotide, due to both reduced incorporation of mismatched nucleotides and reduced propensity to extend partial-length products that have mismatched termini. The improved polymerase is also able to synthesize a broad range of RNA products, including those that require copying templates that are highly structured or contain sequences that previously were difficult to copy.

MethodsUsing a subset of real-world electronic health record (EHR) data from Truveta, a growing collective of health systems that provide more than 18% of all daily clinical care in the US, we identified people who were prescribed a GLP-1-based medication between January 01, 2019 and September 30, 2026. research.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been instrumental in uncovering the genetic basis of complex traits. When integrated with expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) mapping, they can help identify effector genes within GWAS loci through gene regulatory mechanisms. Recent single-cell eQTL (sc-eQTL) studies suggest that genetic effects on gene expression are often cell type- and subtype-specific, providing opportunities to uncover context-specific roles of effector genes that may be obscured in traditional GWAS and eQTL studies in bulk tissues. Here, we leverage results from sc-eQTL mapping in the TenK10K phase 1 project to prioritise effector genes across 69 diseases and 31 biomarker traits, from a total of 12,266 eGenes identified in 28 peripheral immune cell types. Using Mendelian randomisation (MR) and colocalisation, we present a catalogue of predicted effector genes and their estimated directional effects on the trait at cell type resolution, spanning 54,245 associations across 5,270 genes and 28 cell types for disease traits, and 348,103 associations across 9,581 genes and 28 cell types for biomarker traits. By quantifying polygenic enrichment at both the single-cell and cell type levels, we identify distinct immune cell contributions to both immune-related and systemic conditions. We demonstrate differential polygenic enrichment of Crohn's disease and COVID-19 amongst dendritic cell subtypes. Integration with clinical drug development data reveals that therapeutic compounds targeting gene-trait associations identified in this study are twice as likely to have secured regulatory approval. Using Crohn's disease as a motivating example, we demonstrate how population-based sc-eQTL data can pinpoint risk loci, effector genes and cell types, complementing findings from disease-focused tissue samples. Our findings provide a foundational resource for understanding the cell-type-specific genetic architecture of disease and for guiding therapeutic discovery.

research.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading global infectious disease burden. The rising global burden of dysglycemia and dyslipidemia-which geographically converges with TB in many low- and middle-income countries-poses substantial challenges to clinical management. Dysglycemia, encompassing prediabetes and diabetes mellitus, is a well-established risk factor for pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) and adverse treatment outcomes; dyslipidemia frequently co-occurs with dysglycemia, yet its relationship with PTB outcomes is complex and varies by lipid phenotype, timing of measurement, and disease stage. Clinical evidence indicates that in the context of TB-DM, comorbid dyslipidemia is associated with more severe pulmonary pathology, heightened systemic inflammation, and increased risks of drug-induced liver injury (DILI) and mortality, although the overall evidence base remains associative. At the mechanistic level, chronic hyperglycemia and altered lipid metabolism may impair anti-tuberculosis immunity through complementary pathways-including macrophage effector dysfunction, T-cell exhaustion involving the advanced glycation end products (AGEs)-receptor for AGEs (RAGE) axis, and lipid-mediated modulation of inflammatory signaling-although translational evidence from preclinical models to human populations remains limited. This narrative review synthesizes current clinical and mechanistic evidence on the associations between dysglycemia, dyslipidemia, and PTB outcomes, identifies key methodological limitations in the existing literature, and outlines priorities for future research, including prospective longitudinal studies and integrated metabolic profiling, to advance evidence-based management of PTB patients with comorbid metabolic disorders.

research.abstract: Abstract Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, remains a major global health crisis, aggravated by rapid emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug resistant (XDR) strains. Conventional drug discovery is time-consuming and expensive, making computational target identification and drug repurposing as crucial strategies to accelerate the development of novel anti-tubercular therapies. This study aimed to identify and prioritize the metabolic enzymes as potential drug targets through pathway based analysis and to screen the FDA-approved drug library for potential canidates for drug repurposing. Based on the pathway analysis, para-aminobenzoate synthase component I (PabB) was selected as a potential drug target owing to its role in folate biosynthesis. Subesquently, an FDA-approved drug library was screened based on ADMET properties and selected compounds were used for molecular docking agaist the protein. Molecular docking through DiffDock and validation using GNINA revealed that Ligand 5 and Ligand 27 exhibit favourable interaction profiles within the binding region of PabB, and emerged as potential candidates for further investigation in drug repurposing. The identification of PabB protein as an essential metabolic drug target, coupled with screening of FDA-approved drugs as inhibitors, provides a promising framework for anti tubercular drug discovery.

research.abstract: Purpose: To investigate how artificial intelligence (AI) systems detect referable diabetic retinopathy (DR) from retinal photographs by analysing heatmap patterns and determining their overlap with DR features. Methods: Fifty-four AI systems were developed using 27 backbone architectures, with each implemented as both binary-referable and multi-class grading models based on the International Clinical Diabetic Retinopathy (ICDR) grading scale. Models were trained on DDR, BRSET and Kaggle datasets. After training, each model analysed 749 images with DR feature annotations, with Grad-CAM, Integrated Gradients, LIME and SHAP heatmaps generated and compared to pixel-level annotations of microaneurysms, haemorrhages, exudates, cotton wool spots, venous beading, intraretinal microvascular abnormalities and neovascularisation. Results: All models achieved acceptable predictive performance (AUROC >0.8 for most architectures). Heatmap analysis revealed consistent attention to the central and temporal macular region. Exudates and cotton wool spots were highlighted most frequently by the heatmaps, with venous beading and neovascularisation at the disc showing poor overall coverage for binary referable classifiers. Models grading per the ICDR scale demonstrated higher coverage for all features. Substantial variability was observed between architectures, suggesting different feature detection capabilities. Interestingly, the heatmap analysis indicated that the models may be using different features to the ICDR grading scale definitions. Conclusion: AI models do not uniformly correlate with all DR features when detecting referable DR, limiting their predictive performance in unusual presentations. Heatmap aggregation analysis provides a scalable method for analysing model behaviour, allowing strengths and weaknesses to be assessed. These findings may help improve clinician's trust and acceptance of AI.

research.abstract: Abstract Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent, non-apoptotic form of regulated cell death that is driven by lipid peroxidation. In the past decade, it has emerged as a core pathogenic mechanism in a wide range of human diseases, such as neurodegenerative disorders, cardiovascular disease, cancer, and notably, reproductive dysfunction. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms underlying ferroptosis with a specific focus on the System Xc⁻–GSH–GPX4 axis, iron metabolism, lipid peroxidation, and the regulatory roles of key modulators such as Nrf2, ACSL4, and CISD2. This review also explores the physiological roles of ferroptosis in development, tissue homeostasis, and immune regulation, as well as its pathological contributions to obesity, diabetes mellitus, atherosclerosis, neurodegeneration, stroke, cancer, infectious diseases, and reproductive disorders. A substantial part of this review discusses the role of ferroptosis in the pathogenesis of reproductive disorders, such as male reproductive pathologies, including varicocele, testicular ischemia–reperfusion, cryptorchidism, oligospermia, erectile dysfunction, and testicular cancer, and female pathologies like primary ovarian insufficiency, polycystic ovary syndrome, endometriosis, ovarian cancer, and pre-eclampsia. Moreover, the interplay between ferroptosis and immune dysfunction in reproductive tract infections was highlighted. Furthermore, we evaluated current biomarkers, emerging therapeutic strategies, and key translational challenges, highlighting the promise of ferroptosis-modulating agents for novel diagnostic and therapeutic interventions in reproductive medicine and beyond.

research.abstract: Background: Extrapulmonary tuberculosis is an infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that affects organs outside the lungs and presents with diverse clinical manifestations. This study aimed to describe the clinical characteristics of extrapulmonary tuberculosis at dr. Zainoel Abidin General Hospital, Banda Aceh, in 2024. This research employed a descriptive retrospective design using secondary data from medical records of patients diagnosed with extrapulmonary tuberculosis between January and December 2024, using a total sampling technique. A total of 108 subjects met the inclusion criteria. The results showed that most patients were male and within the 19–44-year age group. The most common site of infection was bone tuberculosis, found in 44 subjects (40.7%), followed by lymph nodes and pleura. Molecular rapid testing (TCM) was performed on 43 subjects, with M. tuberculosis detected in 19 subjects (17.6%). The most frequently performed radiological examination was vertebral MRI (37.5%), which demonstrated lesions consistent with bone tuberculosis. Histopathological examination was carried out in 59 subjects, with 42 subjects (38.9%) showing typical features of tuberculosis, including granulomas with caseous necrosis, Langhans giant cells, lymphocytic infiltration, or the presence of TB bacilli. Most patients (91.7%) completed their treatment, and diabetes mellitus (17.6%) was the most common comorbidity. In conclusion, extrapulmonary tuberculosis at dr. Zainoel Abidin General Hospital in 2024 was more prevalent among males of productive age, with bones being the most frequently affected site.

research.abstract: Background: Pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which is transmitted via droplets inhaled by individuals near active TB patients. Meanwhile, diabetes mellitus (DM)is an independent risk factor for TB infection and can increase the risk of latent TB reactivation due to a weakened immune system. The coexistence of TB and DM can impair the absorption of first-line anti-tuberculosis drugs (ATD), making patients more vulnerable to treatment failure, relapse, and increased mortality. Therefore, this study aims to assess the association between glycemic control status and treatment outcomes of first-line ATD therapy. Method: This study used an analytical observational, cross-sectional design and included 86 medical records of pulmonary TB patients with DM, selected through simple random sampling. Bivariate analysis was conducted using the Chi-square test or Fisher’s exact test, with P<0.05 considered statistically significant. Results: Most patients were adults aged 18–59 years (66.3%) and male (55.8%), with the majority having uncontrolled blood glucose levels (75.6%) and normal nutritional status (38.4%). The most common treatment duration was nine months (76.7%). All patients showed clinical improvement and sputum conversion (100%), while 81.4% showed radiological improvement. Bivariate analysis showed a significant difference in radiological improvement between patients with controlled and uncontrolled DM (P=0.009). Conclusion: The majority of pulmonary TB patients with DM were aged 18–59 years, male, and had uncontrolled blood glucose levels. All patients showed clinical improvement and sputum conversion, while 81.4% experienced radiological improvement, with a significant difference between controlled and uncontrolled DM.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Higher resting or sleeping heart rate (HR) has been associated with poorer glucose metabolism in adults without diabetes. However, these associations were estimated across individuals, and within-person characterization of this co-regulation during naturalistic sleep in large free-living cohorts remains limited. Objective This study aimed to determine whether average sleeping HR, an indirect index of cardiac autonomic tone, is associated with nocturnal glucose within a participant and between participants, and whether night-to-night irregularity in sleep duration, sleep onset, and wake time is associated with nocturnal glycemia. Methods In this retrospective observational study, adults who concurrently wore an Ultrahuman Ring and a continuous glucose monitor between January 2024 and June 2025 were analyzed. After participant- and night-level filtering, the cohort comprised 2648 participants from 87 countries, contributing 105,196 paired nights. Each predictor was decomposed into within- and between-participant components by person-mean centering and entered a single linear mixed-effects model with a random intercept for participant, adjusted for age, body mass index (BMI), and sex. Outcomes were nocturnal mean glucose, nocturnal glucose coefficient of variation (CV), and nocturnal time in range (70-110 mg/dL). Per-participant slopes were fitted in participants with sustained wear (at least 30 nights spanning at least 60 days). Estimates were re-derived under trimming and robust-regression specifications and refitted within BMI and regional strata. Results Higher average sleeping HR was associated with higher nocturnal mean glucose both within participants (+5.7 mg/dL per 10 bpm, 95% CI 5.4-5.9) and between participants (+6.5 mg/dL, 95% CI 5.6-7.3; both P <.001). Within participants, higher sleeping HR was also associated with higher glucose CV (+1.37 percentage points, 95% CI 1.30-1.43) and lower time in range (−6.3 percentage points, 95% CI −6.7 to −6.0). Of the 911 sustained-wear participants, 701 (76.9%, 95% CI 74.1%-79.6%) had a positive individual slope (median of +5.2 mg/dL per 10 bpm). The association survived in every BMI stratum and in all 5 regional strata. Sleep-duration irregularity was associated with mean glucose between participants (+4.1 mg/dL per 30 minutes, 95% CI 2.6-5.7) but only weakly within them (+0.23 mg/dL). Within participants, a night 1 standard deviation above a participant’s own mean sleeping HR corresponded to 2.5 mg/dL higher nocturnal mean glucose. Conclusions Average sleeping HR was associated with glucose within individuals as well as between them, indicating that the relationship is not attributable solely to stable between-person differences and reflects, at least in part, night-to-night covariation. The association was modest, but discernible in naturalistic sleep across geographies. Sleep-duration irregularity was associated with nocturnal glycemia mainly between individuals.

research.abstract: Abstract Early screening for glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy (DR) is critical to prevent irreversible vision loss, yet remains inaccessible to many underserved populations. However, AI models trained on hospital-grade fundus images often generalize poorly to low-cost images acquired with portable devices such as smartphones. We proposed CausalFund, a causally inspired learning framework for training AI models that enable reliable low resource screening from easily acquired non-clinical images. CausalFund disentangles disease-relevant retinal features from spurious image factors to achieve domain generalizable screening across clinical and nonclinical settings. We integrated CausalFund with seven deep learning backbones for glaucoma and DR screening from portable-device fundus images, including lightweight architectures suitable for on-device deployment. Across diverse experimental settings and image quality conditions, CausalFund improved smartphone-domain AUC for most backbones while maintaining comparable hospital-domain performance, and achieved a more balanced sensitivity-specificity trade-off than baselines. As a model-agnostic framework, CausalFund could be extended to other diseases and low-resource settings characterized by degraded or non-standard imaging.
